summary: POC scoping for open-model shortlist to support Isobar's clinical summarization + triage assistant. Redwood AE/SE to propose 3 open-model options with quantization and hosting tradeoffs; customer to provide dataset and traffic profile.

transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intro, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Lucas is our SE. Nina: hi, thanks. Samir: hey. Priya: hi. Liam: hello.
[00:28] Maya: Goal today is to scope a POC for your clinical summarization and triage assistant, especially which open models to test, what success looks like, and the benchmarks. Quick high-level: are we looking single-language English or multi?
[00:45] Nina: primarily English, but we do about 20% Spanish notes, some other langs occasionally. So multilingual support is nice to have. Quality is most important — false negatives on triage are a no-go. Latency needs to be reasonable, target p50 under 150ms ideally, p95 under 500ms for end user flows.
[01:10] Lucas: ok that's helpful. Can you share expected QPS and typical token sizes?
[01:18] Priya: average incoming note ~350 tokens, model output ~120 tokens for summaries. For peak, we expect maybe 8–12 QPS, sustained around 3–4 QPS. Concurrency around 30 active users.
[01:35] Maya: good, that helps with sizing. For POC we usually size for 2x expected to be safe. So plan for 20 QPS peak.
[01:50] Samir: what's the cost tradeoff if we pick a bigger open model vs a smaller quantized one?
[01:58] Lucas: rough rule: bigger model increases token cost and latency. For open models we recommend a shortlist: Llama-3-medium 13B (float16), Mistral-7B-v0 (fp16), and a quantized Llama-2-13B-4bit variant for cost. Each has tradeoffs: Llama-3 tends to give stronger clinical reasoning but higher latency; Mistral-7B is fast and cheap but may need prompt engineering for domain accuracy; 4-bit quantized 13B saves cost but may regress on edge-case recall.
[02:30] Nina: we care a lot about domain accuracy — hallucination on medication instructions is unacceptable. How do you evaluate that?
[02:40] Lucas: our benchmark plan: you provide 500 labelled cases (de-identified) across common note types; we'll run automated metrics (ROUGE, exact-match for structured fields) plus human review on a 50-case sample for hallucination. We'll also run latency and cost per 1k token estimates and per-request tail latency.
[03:05] Maya: success criteria capture: quality threshold (F1/recall for entity extraction > 0.90 on key entities, hallucination rate < 2% on samples), latency p50 < 150ms, p95 < 500ms, cost target TBD but we can propose $/1000 tokens thresholds in proposal.
[03:28] Priya: that F1 target sounds fair. One more: audit logs and encryption — we need KMS integration and auditability for traces.
[03:38] Maya: yes, Redwood Private / Dedicated supports KMS and audit logs; for hosted we have SOC2 and can integrate customer-managed keys in Private. We'll include docs.
[03:52] Samir: network wise, we need VPC peering and IP allowlist. Liam will handle.
[03:58] Liam: yep, I'll share firewall requirements.
[04:05] Lucas: on the benchmarking side, recommended tests: 1) quality evaluation on labelled set, 2) latency/cost bench with synthetic QPS ramp (1,5,10,20), 3) GPU profiling for KV cache warm/cold to estimate p95, 4) multilingual spot checks. We'll use Redwood's continuous batching runtime and measure token/sec and tokens per GPU hour.
[04:38] Maya: timeline: if Isobar shares samples by 2026-04-06, we can kick off bench runs week of 2026-04-13 and deliver initial report by 2026-04-17. Does that work?
[04:50] Nina: yes that timeline is good.
[04:55] Priya: for model shortlist, can you write down exact model names and hosting modes?
[05:02] Lucas: sure: 1) Llama-3-13B (fp16) hosted on Redwood Dedicated for stable latency; 2) Mistral-7B-v0 (fp16) hosted on Redwood Hosted API as faster/cheaper baseline; 3) Llama-2-13B-4bit (q4) self-hosted or Redwood Private for lowest cost but more ops. Also we can test Llama-3-7B variant if you want lower latency but might trade quality.
[05:32] Maya: note about fallbacks — our runtime can route to a smaller model on overload. That could help keep p95 down.
[05:40] Samir: curious about end-to-end latency numbers for those models — ballpark?
[05:46] Lucas: ballpark on A100-like or modern GPUs: Mistral-7B p50 ~80–120ms per 120-token output; Llama-3-13B fp16 p50 ~200–350ms; 4-bit 13B depends on kernel optimizations — could be comparable to fp16 in some cases but sometimes higher p95. These are approximate — we'll run exacts in bench.
[06:12] Priya: for multilingual: Spanish support better on Llama-3 than on some Mistral variants?
[06:18] Lucas: generally yes, Llama-3 shows stronger multilingual capabilities OOTB. For critical Spanish flows we might fine-tune or use prompt templates and few-shot examples; we can include spot-checks in the bench.
[06:31] Maya: paperwork: we'll attach SOC2 and security deck, and SSO/SAML options. Also need to know legal timeline for a pilot data processing addendum.
[06:44] Nina: legal can turn around DPA in 2–3 weeks. That works.
[06:50] Samir: also want to measure cost per 1000 tokens for each candidate for our finance team.
[06:56] Lucas: we'll include cost estimates at three traffic levels and run a cost/perf table. Important to call out expected quantization savings and caching impact (prefix caching for repeated templates will help).
[07:12] Priya: do you support user-level rate limiting and routing?
[07:16] Maya: yes, per-route and token-level cost breakdowns in Console, and routing policies for latency vs cost.
[07:24] Liam: question about data residency — some patients in EU, do you have region controls?
[07:30] Maya: yes, Dedicated/Private supports region pinning; hosted can be region-limited and we can discuss placement for EU data.
[07:40] Nina: final recap?
[07:44] Maya: recap: Redwood to send POC proposal with model shortlist + pricing and benchmark plan by 2026-04-07. Isobar to send sample dataset and traffic profile by 2026-04-06. SE deep-dive to run benches week of 2026-04-13; initial report by 2026-04-17. Action items and owners are in the notes.
[08:05] Samir: ok thanks everyone.
[08:08] Call ends with thanks and link to share docs.
notes: Model shortlist final: Llama-3-13B fp16 (quality-biased), Mistral-7B-v0 fp16 (latency/cost baseline), Llama-2-13B q4 (cost-optimized, private). Success criteria: entity F1 >0.90 for key clinical entities, hallucination <2%, p50 <150ms, p95 <500ms. Bench plan incl. labeled set eval + human audit + latency/cost ramps. Timeline: samples by 2026-04-06, bench week of 2026-04-13, report by 2026-04-17. Security: provide SOC2 + KMS options, VPC peering requested.
